In a court order, the judge said it would require “colossal resources” to look at each case individually, and that doing so would not serve the efficiency goals of an MDL. Instead, he issued a series of rulings addressing common issues, ultimately allowing the 800 amended complaints. Defense lawyers counter that federal rules don’t allow such a shortcut, and that the judge was required to consider if each plaintiff individually satisfied Rule 15 and Rule 16. Many do not, they argue. For example, they say the plaintiffs and their lawyers had access to the relevant documents about pharmacy benefit managers as early as July 2018, but failed to act on the information. They also note that in 2020, the Sixth Circuit reversed Polster for a similar procedural move in the opioid MDL, rebuking him for allowing two Ohio counties to add untimely claims. “MDLs are not some kind of judicial border country, where the rules are few and the law rarely makes an appearance,” the panel held . The MDL court “must find efficiencies within the Civil Rules, rather than in violation of them.” Now defense lawyers want the Sixth Circuit again to determine whether Polster crossed the line, and to reinforce its earlier warning that the rules of civil procedure offer no exception for multidistrict litigation. The procedural question prompted a trio of amicus briefs last week in support of the pharmacy benefit managers. The U.S. Chamber of Commerce in its brief warned of potentially “devastating” effects on American businesses and the national economy if MDL judges aren't required to follow the same procedural rules that govern other civil cases. The Chamber also noted that MDLs now account for nearly two-thirds of all private civil litigation at the federal level, writing that they are “the predominant means for suing businesses in federal court today.” Mandamus petitions – where a litigant asks an appeals court to intervene before a case reaches final judgment – are rarely granted. But the pharmacy benefit managers’ protest appears to have piqued the Sixth Circuit’s interest. The appellate court ordered plaintiffs' lawyers, and "invited" Polster, to respond by Sept. 15.

item.title: Is Trump's $5,000 'dividend' legal and how would it work?
item.description: President Donald Trump on Wednesday proposed a $5,000 Trump dividend payment to U.S. adults if his Republicans retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Andy Sullivan, Jonathan Stempel, Saqib Ahmed
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump on Wednesday proposed a [USN:L1N45203G TEXT:"$5,000 "Trump dividend" payment"] to U.S. adults if his Republicans retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections . Here is what we know about Trump's pledge: WHO WOULD GET THE MONEY AND WHERE WOULD IT COME FROM? Trump said the checks would go to all adult U.S. citizens -- about 240 million people, according to the U.S. Census. That would cost a total of $1.2 trillion. Vice President JD Vance suggested on Fox News after Trump's speech that the U.S. government could draw on tariff revenue, which has been juiced by Trump's trade wars . The Congressional Budget Office estimates the government has taken in $167 billion so far in the fiscal year that ends September 30 -- not nearly enough to cover the cost of Trump's proposed giveaway. The payments would instead widen the government's budget gap, which is already at a level that [USN:S0N43F052 TEXT:"alarms budget watchdogs"]. CBO estimates the government will spend $2.1 trillion more than it collects in revenue in the current fiscal year and projects that figure will grow in the years to come as the population ages. WOULD THE PAYMENTS BE LEGAL? Candidates regularly promise benefits in return for votes. During the 2024 presidential campaign, Trump promised tax breaks for seniors, tipped workers and other targeted groups —and delivered them in his "One Big Beautiful Bill" the following year. Democratic candidates, including President-elect Joe Biden, promised a third round of COVID-19 relief checks in a Georgia special election in 2021 and delivered when they won control of Congress. The U.S. Supreme Court has ruled that a comparable promise is legal. In a unanimous 1982 decision, the high court overturned a lower-court ruling that had invalidated the election of a Kentucky official who had promised to save taxpayer money by lowering county commissioners' salaries. Elon Musk, the world's richest person, [USN:L6N42X16V TEXT:"offered voters a chance to win $1 million"] in 2024 if they signed a petition to support the Constitution. That drew legal challenges, still unresolved, from voters who said they had no real chance to win because Musk was seeking people to support his political action committee, which backed Republican candidates. It would be difficult to challenge Trump's dividend in court, as voters might have trouble showing that they had been directly harmed. WOULD THIS HAVE TO PASS CONGRESS? Yes. Congress has authority over spending under the U.S. Constitution. Trump's Republicans control both the House and the Senate by narrow margins, and several members of his party have already reacted favorably to the idea. Democrats would be sure to oppose any legislation and could block passage in the Senate, where a supermajority of 60 votes is needed to advance most legislation. Republicans could invoke a complex budget process to bypass Democrats and approve the bill along party lines. They have successfully used this approach twice since Trump's January 2025 return to office, but have struggled to advance a third such package. They have little time to act before the November 3 elections, as the House is scheduled to be in session for only one week before then. Congress could also try to act in a "lame-duck" session after the election. HAS THE U.S. GOVERNMENT GIVEN MONEY DIRECTLY TO CITIZENS BEFORE? Yes. Congress approved three separate direct payments in March 2020, December 2020 and March 2021 as part of sweeping relief packages to help people weather the economic disruption from the COVID-19 pandemic. Those payments — up to $1,200, $600 and $1,400 per adult, respectively — were phased out for higher-income people. That amounted to 476 million payments totaling $814 billion, according to a congressional oversight committee. Investigators found numerous logistical problems, including fraud and $1.4 billion sent to dead people. HOW WOULD THIS AFFECT THE ECONOMY AND FINANCIAL MARKETS? Economic studies have shown that the pandemic-era stimulus checks contributed to the subsequent rise in inflation by substantially boosting consumer demand. Those payments also boosted the stock market, with a measurable spike in retail trading volumes following each wave of stimulus deposits. But Trump's proposed dividend could upend bond markets if the government funded it through borrowing. The massive influx of new Treasury debt, combined with revived inflation fears, could drive bond prices sharply lower and send yields soaring. That could push government borrowing costs higher, further pressuring the U.S. budget at a time when interest payments already exceed military spending. Yields on [USN:L4N4520VC TEXT:"benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds"] ticked up to 4.91% on Thursday as investors assessed Trump's proposal. HAS TRUMP MADE SIMILAR PROMISES IN THE PAST? Trump promised a similar $2,000 dividend in November 2025 tied to tariff revenue and said it would not apply to wealthy people, though no follow-up action was taken. Trump successfully sent a one-time "warrior dividend" payment of $1,776 to roughly 1.45 million military members in December 2025, drawing on money already approved by Congress. On Thursday, Trump's White House said nearly 1 million Americans will get [USN:FWN4520NI TEXT:"$500 payments"] to account for what it describes as excess fees charged for Affordable Care Act health insurance.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for financial services industry
item.description: OpenAI on Thursday launched a version of ChatGPT built for the financial services industry, combining its latest AI model with built-in data from providers including LSEG , PitchBook and Daloopa to target investment bankers and equity researchers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OpenAI on Thursday launched a version of ChatGPT built for the financial services industry, combining its latest AI model with built-in data from providers including LSEG (LSEG.L) , PitchBook and Daloopa to target investment bankers and equity researchers. The product, ChatGPT for Financial Services, was developed with Morgan Stanley (MS.N) and Evercore (EVR.N) as design partners to help shape the offering, OpenAI said in a blog post. The launch reflects a broader push by AI companies to build products for regulated industries where data governance and security are central concerns. The product builds on ChatGPT Enterprise's existing security controls, including role-based access and encryption, and allows compliance teams to export workspace logs into audit workflows. The service is powered by GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's newest model, which the company said was built to improve retrieval across financial data tools, financial reasoning and the accuracy of generated content. Users can conduct research across multiple sources, build financial models and generate client materials such as pitchbooks using their firm's own templates, OpenAI said. OpenAI said it plans to expand the breadth of financial data available through the product and further train its models to identify, interpret and apply that information across tasks traditionally handled by experienced analysts. The product includes datasets from Daloopa, LSEG News, PitchBook, Crunchbase, Quartr and others covering earnings transcripts, financial statements and company fundamentals. OpenAI said the data is indexed on its own infrastructure to improve retrieval and citation. LSEG serves as the sole distributor of Reuters news, financial data, and real-time alerts to global financial professionals. Firms that already hold data subscriptions can connect them through integrations with FactSet (FDS.N) , S&P Global, Preqin and Datasite, the company said. OpenAI said it plans to expand the product beyond investment banking and equity research across the wider financial services sector.

item.title: Peru to join US anti-drug coalition 'Shield of the Americas' after Rubio visit
item.description: Peru will join the U.S.-led "Shield of the Americas" coalition against drug cartels, President Keiko Fujimori said on Thursday during U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit, deepening cooperation and tightening security ties with Washington early in her presidency.
item.dc:creator: Marco Aquino
item.content:encoded: Peru will join the U.S.-led "Shield of the Americas" coalition against drug cartels, President [USN:L6N43Q0ZQ TEXT:"Keiko Fujimori"] said on Thursday during U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit, deepening cooperation and tightening security ties with Washington early in her presidency. Speaking at a joint news conference, Fujimori said Peru's participation in the coalition would speed intelligence-sharing and bolster joint action against criminal groups operating across borders. Rubio welcomed Lima's decision, saying the initiative was meant to "shield the region" from organizations that threaten the sovereignty of countries across the hemisphere. He reiterated that the region was a priority for Washington. "U.S. getting involved in the region is not a favor. It is essential to our own security, to our own prosperity, to our own well-being in America. And this administration is committed to this," he said, adding there would be more similar initiatives. The top U.S. diplomat's trip to Peru, the last stop of a three-country swing to Latin America that also included Ecuador and Colombia, is the highest-level U.S. visit to the country since President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025. The visit, which focused on counternarcotics, migration and trade, comes as Washington seeks closer security and commercial ties with conservative governments in Latin America while pushing back against China's influence in mining and infrastructure. Peru is the world's third-largest copper producer. The two countries have already moved to deepen defense ties. In January, the United States designated Peru a major non-NATO ally, and the State Department approved a possible $1.5 billion foreign military sale for design and construction work at Callao Naval Base, Peru's main naval hub. "We appreciate this opportunity (to join the initiative), because for us, having previously had to tackle terrorism, (we) know how difficult it is to confront criminality today," Fujimori said. She was apparently referring to the period of political violence driven by the Maoist Shining Path insurgency that her father, former President Alberto Fujimori, cracked down on during his decade in power from 1990 to 2000. Peru's [USN:S0N42A02L TEXT:"Foreign Ministry"] had flagged in recent months that Lima might join the Shield of the Americas as part of a broader push to strengthen border security and coordination against transnational crime. Officials also discussed U.S. support for Peru's preparations for a possible emergency related to the El Niño weather phenomenon, Fujimori said. Rubio's trip coincided with the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, where Trump hopes to energize core supporters and help the party hold onto its congressional majorities. 'NOT ANYONE'S BACKYARD' Peruvian government sources said the country was also seeking relief from U.S. tariffs after Trump raised duties in late July to 12.5% from 10% on imports from 60 trading partners, including Peru, citing failures to stop imports involving forced labor. While Peru has traded largely tariff-free under a 2009 agreement, the new duties have hit Peru's agricultural exports, specifically blueberries, grapes and avocados. As Lima negotiates the removal of those duties, China continues to outpace the United States in trade with Peru. Peru's trade with China rose 35% in the first half of the year, surpassing a 20% increase in trade with the U.S., according to official data. The figures put bilateral trade with China on track to surpass the more than $50 billion recorded in 2025, compared with roughly $19 billion in trade with the United States that year. China's embassy in Peru defended its trade and political ties this week ahead of Rubio's visit. Beijing operates copper mines and has expanded its footprint in Peru's energy and infrastructure sectors. "The Western Hemisphere is not anyone's 'backyard'," the Chinese embassy in Lima said late on Tuesday on X.

item.title: In-house counsel group accuses rival of training AI on its materials
item.description: The Association of Corporate Counsel, a nonprofit bar association for in-house attorneys, sued competitor The L Suite in Delaware federal court on Thursday for allegedly copying its materials to train a lawyer-focused chatbot.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: The Association of Corporate Counsel, a nonprofit bar association for in-house attorneys, sued competitor The L Suite in Delaware federal court on Thursday for allegedly copying its materials to train a lawyer-focused chatbot. The lawsuit said that The L Suite trained its chatbot Lloyd on copyrighted works including at least one ACC report, and that it "brazenly" promoted Lloyd with an image of the report and an ACC trademark. Spokespeople for The L Suite did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the complaint. "We made a good-faith effort to resolve this matter directly, and when that effort failed, filing this complaint became necessary to protect our members’ interests and the integrity of ACC’s work," ACC president Jason Brown said in a statement. The Washington-based ACC has more than 48,000 members and publishes content, including continuing legal education materials, surveys and white papers. The L Suite, which calls itself "the leading general counsel community on its website," announced the launch of its Lloyd chatbot in May. The L Suite said in a press release that Lloyd "combines foundational AI capabilities with the trusted judgment of thousands of accomplished in-house legal executives." The ACC said in its complaint that an L Suite video promoting Lloyd displayed the cover of an ACC report. "As a result, there can be no doubt that The L Suite was specifically aware that its Lloyd platform was utilizing ACC materials," the lawsuit said. The ACC also alleged that The L Suite violated its trademark rights in the phrase "By In-House Counsel, For In-House Counsel" by using "Built By In-House Counsel, For In-House Counsel" in its Lloyd advertising. The ACC requested monetary damages and a court order blocking The L Suite from using its trademarks and copyrighted materials. The case is Association of Corporate Counsel v. The L Suite Inc, U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, No. 1:26-cv-01138. For the ACC: Robert Leighton and Paul Sauerteig of Goldberg Kohn For The L Suite: attorney information not yet available

item.title: Groups sue Trump administration to revive environmental grants in Democratic-leaning states
item.description: Organizations that had received federal funding for environmental projects have filed a lawsuit alleging that the U.S. Department of Energy unconstitutionally terminated nearly 300 grants worth billions of dollars due to the recipients residing in states that tend to vote for Democratic candidates.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: Organizations that had received federal funding for environmental projects have filed a lawsuit alleging that the U.S. Department of Energy unconstitutionally terminated nearly 300 grants worth billions of dollars due to the recipients residing in states that tend to vote for Democratic candidates. Plaintiffs ranging from a sustainable cement production company to a California-based non-profit filed the class action lawsuit on Wednesday in federal court in Boston. Their lawsuit takes aim at a decision by the Energy Department during the most recent government shutdown in October 2025 to terminate grants that largely supported projects promoting environmentally friendly energy. The grantees were informed in termination letters that their funding was being halted because the grants do "not effectuate the Department of Energy’s priorities of ensuring affordable, reliable, and abundant energy," the lawsuit said. But the complaint said that in the year since, the Trump administration stipulated in three other lawsuits that a primary reason the grants were terminated was that the grantee at issue was located in a "blue state." The earlier lawsuits had focused on a subset of the terminated grants, unlike Wednesday's case, which seeks class action status and an order declaring all the remaining grant terminations unconstitutional. The plaintiffs in Wednesday's lawsuit argue that the Energy Department violated the U.S. Constitution's First and Fifth Amendments by intentionally treating grant recipients differently based on where they were located and the political entities with which they chose to associate. "Defendants took adverse action against Plaintiffs and Class members because of their association with disfavored political entities," the complaint said. "Defendants would not have terminated these awards but for that protected association." An Energy Department spokesperson in a statement said: "None of the termination decisions were based on political considerations." During the shutdown, Trump repeatedly threatened to target perceived Democratic interests and priorities for cuts, and White House budget director Russell Vought announced on social media the termination of nearly $8 billion in funding "to fuel the Left’s climate agenda." A subsequent post by Vought, the director of the Office of Management and Budget, said those projects were in 16 states that voted for now-former Vice President Kamala Harris, a Democrat, over Trump in the 2024 presidential election. Those states included California and New York. The lawsuit said that ultimately 284 grants were terminated and that, with one exception, all of the recipients had been in states that voted for Harris and had two Democratic-caucusing senators. The plaintiffs include Furno Materials, a California-based company focused on sustainable cement production that had received a $20 million grant; Coonamessett Farm Foundation, a Massachusetts-based research foundation which lost a $3.5 million grant; and the California Green Building Council, which had been previously awarded $3.8 million. The case is Furno Materials v Wright, U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts, No. 1:26-cv-14131. For the plaintiffs: Emma Lerner Freeman of Lerner Freeman Law; Jamie Crooks of Fairmark Partners; and Gabriel Daly of Roselle LLP

item.title: Nubank inicia serviços nos EUA por conta poupança, cartões e remessa
item.description: O Nubank começou nesta quinta-feira a oferecer produtos financeiros nos Estados Unidos por meio de bancos parceiros, anunciou o banco digital brasileiro em comunicado.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Bautzer, Andre Romani
item.content:encoded: O Nubank (NU.N) começou nesta quinta-feira a oferecer produtos financeiros nos Estados Unidos por meio de bancos parceiros, anunciou o banco digital brasileiro em comunicado. Os produtos iniciais serão contas de poupança, cartões de crédito e remessas de valores, afirmaram o presidente-executivo, David Vélez, e a cofundadora e presidente-executiva do Nubank nos EUA, Cristina Junqueira, durante um evento em Miami. O Nubank fez parceria com o Lead Bank para oferecer contas de depósito com rendimento de 3,50%, além de transferências de dinheiro e um cartão de crédito sem taxas com 1,5% de cashback. A licença bancária do Nubank foi aprovada condicionalmente pelo OCC em janeiro e agora o banco está passando pelo processo de aprovação do Federal Reserve e da FDIC. Junqueira disse durante o evento de lançamento em Miami que o Nubank começará a operar nos EUA no próximo ano. Enquanto isso, o banco vai operar por meio de um modelo de parceria. A ação do banco em Nova York subia 0,3% às 16h43 (horário de Brasília), cotada a US$15,04. No futuro, os clientes também poderão negociar ativos digitais, incluindo bitcoin e ethereum. Outros produtos que o Nubank estuda oferecer nos EUA são investimentos, seguros e contas para pequenas empresas, disse Vélez em entrevista à Reuters no início desta semana. Vélez afirmou que o acesso a serviços bancários para os clientes nos EUA é melhor do que na América Latina, onde, anos atrás, uma grande parcela da população não tinha conta em banco. No entanto, milhões de pessoas ainda têm acesso restrito ao crédito e utilizam produtos com taxas elevadas. Inicialmente, o Nubank terá como público-alvo clientes jovens, mais habituados a serviços digitais, e a população hispânica dos EUA, mais familiarizada com a marca que já opera no Brasil, no México e na Colômbia. O crescimento orgânico é a principal estratégia nos EUA, mas Vélez afirmou que o Nubank está atento a possíveis oportunidades para acelerar o crescimento por meio de aquisições. O executivo disse que levará "vários anos" para que a operação nos EUA se torne lucrativa. No Brasil, seu maior mercado, o Nubank levou oito anos para alcançar a lucratividade. O lucro líquido total da empresa ultrapassou US$1 bilhão e superou as estimativas do mercado no segundo trimestre.

item.title: Saudi wealth fund weighs EA-Savvy merger, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: Saudi Arabia's wealth fund is considering merging Electronic Arts with Savvy Games to create a gaming giant, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia's wealth fund is considering merging Electronic Arts with Savvy Games to create a gaming giant, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. The merger of the two companies, both controlled by the Public Investment Fund, would create a gaming behemoth spanning franchises, including EA Sports FC, Battlefield and The Sims, and Savvy-owned mobile hits such as Monopoly Go! and Pokemon GO. PIF had acquired EA through a consortium for roughly $55 billion last month and taken the videogame publisher private. A final decision on the two companies' merger has not been reached and a deal is unlikely to happen until Savvy completes its $6-billion acquisition of Chinese mobile gaming business Moonton, the report added. Electronic Arts and Savvy Games did not immediately respond to requests for comment, while Saudi PIF declined to comment. Any combination, however, could face antitrust scrutiny as regulators have taken a close look at large gaming-sector transactions in recent years, including Microsoft's (MSFT.O) acquisition of Activision Blizzard. The deliberations come as the gaming industry grapples with a post-pandemic slowdown, cost cuts and layoffs, while companies pursue scale and durable recurring revenue. Savvy's CEO Brian Ward stepped down last week after overseeing the Saudi-backed group's global investment and acquisition push.

item.title: Washington nonprofit Better Markets sues Federal Reserve over capital rule overhaul
item.description: Better Markets, a Washington nonprofit that advocates for Wall Street reforms, sued the U.S. Federal Reserve and its top regulatory official on Thursday, alleging the central bank mishandled a sweeping overhaul of its capital regulations.
item.dc:creator: Pete Schroeder, Michelle Price
item.content:encoded: Better Markets, a Washington nonprofit that advocates for Wall Street reforms, sued the U.S. Federal Reserve and its top regulatory official on Thursday, alleging the central bank mishandled a sweeping overhaul of its capital regulations. The unusual lawsuit filed in Washington, D.C., signals a growing backlash against the Trump administration's effort to scale back a raft of what regulatory advocates say are essential supervisory and regulatory financial system safeguards. It alleges that private interactions the Fed's vice chair for supervision, Michelle Bowman, held with Wall Street banks about an open public consultation on major capital rules "corrupted" the federal rulemaking process, depriving Better Markets of due process under the Fifth Amendment. The lawsuit leans on notice-and-comment requirements and other safeguards associated with the Administrative Procedure Act as evidence that the process was tainted. It cites [USN:L4N4101DQ TEXT:"April reporting by Reuters"] that Bowman told banking executives that she did not expect the industry, which fought aggressively for the Fed to overhaul its original 2023 capital plan, to stage another major pushback in an attempt to win further capital relief. It also cites a report by Bloomberg that she privately "told Wall Street leaders to support capital plans that are widely seen as a win for industry and stop asking for carve outs." The lawsuit alleges that the undisclosed interactions violated restrictions on private communications in federal rulemakings. In doing so, Bowman violated Better Markets' right to meaningfully participate in and comment on the rule, the group alleges. PROPOSED CAPITAL CHANGES UNDER REVIEW A spokesperson for the Fed did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Bowman, who has been leading the changes, has previously said her goal is to streamline regulations and oversight to make them more sensitive to real risks. The Fed in March [USN:L6N406104 TEXT:"proposed changes to the Basel, GSIB surcharge and other related rules"], which determine funds big banks must put aside to absorb potential losses, which would result in capital falling for the affected lenders by 4.8% in aggregate. The rule was subject to a public consultation which ended in June and is not yet finalized. "This is not just some technical dispute about process," Better Markets CEO Dennis Kelleher said in a statement. "The corruption alleged here was to rig the rules related to bank capital, which are critical financial stability rulemakings." While Wall Street groups have frequently sued federal regulators, litigation against the Fed over rulemakings is rare. Big banks in 2024 under the former Democratic administration sued the central bank over its [USN:L4N3NP0MX TEXT:"annual "stress test""] health checks and [USN:L1N3EQ380 TEXT:"fair lending rules"], but those lawsuits were the first in recent memory, according to a Reuters analysis at the time and academic Fed-watchers.

item.title: US and France on collision course after World Cup quarter-final wins
item.description: After cruising to quarter-final victories at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on Thursday, the U.S. and France have set off on a collision course that could bring a rematch of their 2024 Olympic gold-medal game in the final.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: After cruising to quarter-final victories at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on Thursday, the U.S. and France have set off on a collision course that could bring a rematch of their 2024 Olympic gold-medal game in the final. France dispatched China 90-61 in Berlin to reach the semi-finals for the first time, led by 15 points each from Janelle Salaun and Marine Johannes, as well as 14 from captain Gabby Williams. They now have a chance to claim their first World Cup medal since the inaugural tournament in 1953, when they finished third in the final round. France will face Germany in the first semi-final on Saturday. The U.S. will play Spain later that day. "This team here just want to make a new story and I think that's the most important thing," France coach Jean Aime Toupane told reporters. U.S. SET RECORDS IN BEATING HUNGARY After missing out on Olympic gold to the Americans by one point in Paris two years ago, France entered the tournament with confidence and hunger. "We are lucky because we are a group that have known each other for a couple of years now," Salaun said of the team's chemistry. "We went through a lot of things, the Olympics, training camp(s), so we just know each other and we know what we want. We have a goal and we want to do everything to get to this goal." Both Olympic finalists are now one win away from setting up a rematch after the U.S. crushed Hungary 108-56 earlier in the day, with 19 points from Napheesa Collier. The defending champions' 108 points and 31 assists were both records for a World Cup quarter-final. "This was one of our most complete performances of the tournament," U.S. coach Kara Lawson said, adding that she was pleased with her team's defensive efforts. "And then offensively, we as coaches love when they share the ball," Lawson said with a smile. "And they did at just a high level." "As far as France, what a wonderful team, and they've had an outstanding World Cup so far," Lawson added. "So they should have a lot of people thinking that they can do well."

item.title: UK retailers stock charcoal linked to Paraguay deforestation, group says
item.description: Major British retailers, including B&Q and Waitrose, are selling barbecue charcoal from trees cleared to create more farmland in Paraguay's Gran Chaco, according to an investigation published on Thursday by advocacy group Global Witness.
item.dc:creator: Iñigo Alexander, Daniela Desantis
item.content:encoded: Major British retailers, including B&Q and Waitrose, are selling barbecue charcoal from trees cleared to create more farmland in Paraguay's Gran Chaco , according to an investigation published on Thursday by advocacy group Global Witness. The report traces charcoal sold in UK supermarkets and hardware stores to the Paraguayan forestry company Taruma. Global Witness says Taruma is the largest international supplier of British barbecue brand Big K, whose products are sold across the country. The subtropical dry forest of Gran Chaco, South America's second-largest forested region after the Amazon rainforest, stretches across Paraguay, Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia. In response, a Waitrose spokesperson said all the charcoal it sells complies with standards set by the Forest Stewardship Council, an independent forest certification system. B&Q did not respond to requests for comment. Paraguay has been seeking closer trade ties with Europe through the [USN:L6N41B0RR TEXT:"EU-Mercosur agreement"], at a time of [USN:L1N44V0U0 TEXT:"growing scrutiny"] of the environmental impact of imports from the South American bloc that includes Paraguay, Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay. Satellite analysis cited in the report found that Taruma sources its wood from ranches that since 2012 have cleared more than 28,000 hectares (69,000 acres) of forest. A second supplier, Paben SA, which worked with Big K until 2023, has cleared roughly 2,700 hectares of forest in the Paraguayan Chaco since 2021, the report said. Paben SA did not respond to requests for comment. In a written response to Reuters, Taruma denied wrongdoing. "Taruma does not clear forest and holds no clearing permits, so our operations do not add to deforestation or to its effects on the regional climate. Our sustainability team follows the research on Chaco land-use change closely," Chief Executive Rahmeen Farudi said. Researchers, including NASA scientists, have said Paraguay has one of the world's highest deforestation rates relative to forest cover, driven largely by farming and cattle ranching. Paraguay, a major [USN:L4N3R11PX TEXT:"grains"] and meat exporter, unveiled in July its first national forestry policy, acknowledging decades of state-driven deforestation for agriculture. The government pledged to move toward stricter environmental monitoring to meet EU trade standards. While Britain is no longer part of the EU, the sale of charcoal to the UK may hurt Paraguay's ambitions to sell other products to the EU under an eventual trade deal with Mercosur. Paraguay's National Forestry Institute did not respond to requests for comment. DEFORESTATION, LEGISLATION AND TRADE Global Witness said that both Paraguay's permissive environmental laws and the UK's "flawed" environmental legislation allow deforestation-linked charcoal to reach the British market. Britain's 2021 Environment Act bans imports linked to illegal deforestation. It applies only to products sourced from illegally deforested land and does not cover charcoal products. This means Paraguayan goods produced on legally cleared land can still enter the UK. Starting on December 30, the EU will have stricter rules banning all products linked to deforested land regardless of whether the clearing was legal. The UK's Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, known as Defra, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Environmental groups and several [USN:L6N43314Q TEXT:"EU governments"], including France, Austria and [USN:L8N4171DL TEXT:"Poland"], have warned that extending Mercosur's agricultural exports to Europe could accelerate deforestation in ecosystems such as the Gran Chaco.

item.title: Portuguese group D3 sues Meta, TikTok and YouTube over addictive design
item.description: Portuguese digital rights group D3 has filed lawsuits against Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, accusing them of designing features in their platforms that keep users hooked, it said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves
item.content:encoded: Portuguese digital rights group D3 has filed lawsuits against Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, accusing them of designing features in their platforms that keep users hooked, it said on Thursday. The four collective actions, which allow associations to bring cases on behalf of a broader group of consumers, follow on from lawsuits in other countries that have challenged [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"social media's addictive design"]. A spokesperson for Alphabet's Google (GOOGL.O) , owner of YouTube, said providing people with "a safer, healthier experience has always been core to our work" and pointed to tools such as "take a break" and bedtime reminders designed to help users manage viewing habits. "We'll be assessing this case and responding in due course," the spokesperson said. Meta (META.O) , owner of Facebook and Instagram, and TikTok owner ByteDance did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Filed by law firm Andersen Tax & Legal Iberia with Lisbon's Civil Court between April and May and disclosed only now after the judicial summer break, the legal action seeks to "hold these platforms accountable and force them to provide a safe experience for their users," D3 said. D3 highlighted features including infinite scrolling, autoplay videos, persistent notifications and highly personalised recommendation systems. By removing natural breaks in usage, constantly serving personalised content and repeatedly prompting users to return, platforms create behavioural feedback loops akin to techniques long used in the gambling industry, D3 said. "Platforms do not have to be hyper-addictive," D3 President Ricardo Lafuente said. "A healthy, productive and educational social media ecosystem is possible, but only if the rules are robust, properly enforced and directed at those who persist in ignoring them," he said. On both sides of the Atlantic, social media has come under mounting scrutiny. In February, TikTok was [USN:L8N3Z216K TEXT:"charged under EU rules"] over allegedly addictive features, while in August Meta agreed to pay [USN:L4N44N1N4 TEXT:"up to $18 billion"] to settle U.S. addiction claims. According to data aggregated by website SocialMediaTransparency.org, the four platforms had a combined reach of 33 million monthly users in Portugal in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Rendimientos en EEUU suben por inflación y subida del petróleo que refuerzan apuesta a alzas de tasas
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron el jueves después de que se conocieron datos de inflación que impulsaron las expectativas de un alza de las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal la próxima semana, mientras que el repunte de los precios del petróleo también avivó el temor inflación.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron el jueves después de que se conocieron datos de inflación que impulsaron las expectativas de un alza de las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal la próxima semana, mientras que el repunte de los precios del petróleo también avivó el temor inflación. Los rendimientos también prolongaron su tendencia alcista después de que el Gobierno estadounidense anunció la recompra de bonos por valor de 5.200 millones de dólares para respaldar la liquidez del mercado, una cantidad inferior al límite de 6.000 millones de dólares y que representa solo la mitad de los 10.500 millones de dólares en bonos ofrecidos en la operación. La rentabilidad de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años alcanzó sus niveles más altos desde finales de 2023, mientras que la de los bonos a 30 años llegó a máximos desde 2007 y la de los bonos a 2 años alcanzó sus niveles más altos en más de dos años. Los rendimientos a largo plazo redujeron sus ganancias tras una exitosa subasta gubernamental de bonos a 30 años, pero el repunte fue efímero, ya que los futuros del petróleo extendieron su tendencia alcista. Datos mostraron que el índice de precios al productor (IPP) de Estados Unidos aumentó en línea con las expectativas mensuales. En los 12 meses a agosto, el incremento fue del 5,4%, frente a las expectativas del consenso del 5,3% y un aumento del 4,8% en julio. Los precios de la energía subieron un 4,2% en agosto, tras dos meses consecutivos de descenso. Tras la publicación de los datos, los operadores apostaban por una probabilidad de aproximadamente el 70% de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas de interés 25 puntos básicos en su reunión del 15 y 16 de septiembre, frente al 62% anterior, según los datos de probabilidades de tasas de interés de LSEG. A la preocupación por la inflación se sumó un repunte de aproximadamente el 6% en los precios del petróleo, con ambos índices de referencia cotizando por encima de los 100 dólares. Los ataques contra el transporte marítimo alimentaron la inquietud de los operadores de que haya más interrupciones del ya escaso suministro energético. El presidente Donald Trump dijo que esperaba que la guerra con Irán termine tras las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre. La rentabilidad de los bonos estadounidenses de referencia a 10 años subió 10,93 puntos básicos, al 4,946%, alcanzando sus niveles más altos desde octubre de 2023. El retorno del bono a 30 años subió 7,27 puntos básicos, al 5,3587%, su nivel más alto desde junio de 2007. La rentabilidad de los bonos a dos años, que normalmente se mueve al ritmo de las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal, subió 13,33 puntos básicos, al 4,56%, alcanzando su nivel más alto desde julio de 2024.

item.title: Trump administration proposes axing grace period for H-1B visa holders after job loss
item.description: The Trump administration has proposed eliminating a 60-day grace period that allows certain immigrants, including skilled workers on H-1B visas, to stay in the United States and find a new sponsor after losing their job, according to a government notice posted online on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Susan Heavey
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has proposed eliminating a 60-day grace period that allows certain immigrants, including skilled workers on H-1B visas, to stay in the United States and find a new sponsor after losing their job, according to a government notice posted online on Thursday. Under the planned rule change, published in the Federal Register by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, those with [USN:L1N44M0MZ TEXT:"H-1B"] and certain other temporary work visas would have to leave the country as soon as their employment ends — a potential blow to top American tech companies that rely heavily on foreign workers. It is the latest step by U.S. President Donald Trump to limit legal immigration since returning to office in January 2025. His administration has also introduced [USN:L1N44H0LJ TEXT:"higher visa fees"] for skilled workers and recently [USN:L8N44S1Z3 TEXT:"paused immigrant visa appointments"] at U.S. missions globally while it implements a new training program. Companies affected by the change could see some disruption, DHS wrote in its proposal, but it said the jobs could go to American workers instead. In some situations, immigrant workers who leave could potentially reapply if their employer petitions for them, it added. "DHS presumes that they will either offer the same jobs to equally qualified U.S. workers or go through the I-129 petition process depending on their workforce requirement," the notice said. The 60-day grace period, in place since 2017, allows foreign workers time to find another U.S. job or get their affairs in order — whether selling a home or pulling children out of school — before leaving the country. "Many H-1B workers have been here for years, and they and their families have established themselves in their communities," said Gabriel Chin, a professor at the UC Davis School of Law. "I see no legitimate reason to force them to leave because they are changing jobs." VISAS CRITICAL FOR TECH COMPANIES H-1B visas, established by Congress in 1990, are especially critical for tech companies seeking talent from India and China, allowing them to fill roles where there is sometimes a lack of qualified U.S. workers. Consultancy companies such as Deloitte, PwC and Ernst & Young as well as outsourcing firms such as Tata Consultancy Services TCS.NS , Infosys INFY.NS , HCL Tech HCLT.NS and LTIMindtree LTIM.NS are [USN:L3N3V90SB TEXT:"top H-1B sponsors"]. Lawyers for Berardi Immigration Law, which specializes in business-related immigration issues, said the move would "sharply compress the timeline HR teams have to manage layoffs and offboarding for foreign national employees." “It seems like every week this administration announces a new step to make life more difficult for immigrants in the U.S. and the companies and communities that rely on them," said Todd Schulte, president of FWD.us, an immigration advocacy group. If implemented, the change would also apply to E-1 international trader visa holders; E-2 commercial vehicle operator visa holders; L-1 short-term work for executives or managers with international companies; O-1 visas for people "with an extraordinary ability" in science, sports or the arts; and TN professional workers. It would also affect H-1B1 skilled worker visa holders from Singapore and Chile and E-3 specialty worker visa holders from Australia. The rule is subject to a two-month public comment period before it can be finalized.

item.title: S&P 500 cae ante subida de rendimientos de los bonos y preocupación por inflación
item.description: Las bolsas estadounidenses cerraron a la baja el jueves después de que los datos sobre los precios al productor de agosto y la subida de los precios del petróleo avivaran los temores de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas de interés la próxima semana, mientras que el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro restó atractivo a las acciones.
item.dc:creator: Niket Nishant, Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: Las bolsas estadounidenses cerraron a la baja el jueves después de que los datos sobre los precios al productor de agosto y la subida de los precios del petróleo avivaran los temores de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas de interés la próxima semana, mientras que el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro restó atractivo a las acciones. *Los gigantes del sector de los semiconductores perdieron terreno, y Nvidia (NVDA.O) y Micron Technology (MU.O) lastraron el S&P 500. Apple (AAPL.O) repuntó un día después de lanzar un iPhone de 1.999 dólares. *Dado que las rutas de suministro a través del estrecho de Ormuz y del mar Rojo se vieron interrumpidas por la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, el crudo Brent subió un 6% hasta los 107 dólares el barril, lo que agravó los temores inflacionistas y avivó las expectativas de que la Fed suba las tasas de interés en su reunión de política monetaria del miércoles. *Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años subieron hasta su nivel más alto en casi tres años, mientras que los de los bonos a 30 años alcanzaron su máximo en más de 19 años y los de los bonos a 2 años llegaron a su nivel más alto en más de dos años. *"Los rendimientos están subiendo en el extremo corto de la curva porque es probable que la Fed suba las tasas en los próximos meses. Los rendimientos están subiendo en el extremo largo de la curva debido a los problemas de deuda y déficit, y a una inflación persistente", afirmó Ross Mayfield, analista de estrategia de inversión de Baird en Louisville, Kentucky. *"El aumento de los rendimientos es negativo para el mercado de valores. Reduce las valoraciones y encarece el funcionamiento de las empresas, además de encarecer la vida de los consumidores". *Los datos publicados el jueves mostraron que el índice de precios al productor (IPP) de Estados Unidos aumentó en agosto, en línea con las expectativas, en términos mensuales, en un contexto de repunte del costo de los productos energéticos. Los inversionistas prestarán especial atención a los datos de precios al consumo de agosto que se publicarán el viernes. *Según los datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 44,16 puntos, o un 0,58 %, hasta cerrar en 7.592,20 puntos, mientras que el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) perdió 167,15 puntos, o un 0,64 %, hasta situarse en 26.086,19. El Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) cayó 313,64 puntos, o un 0,60 %, hasta situarse en 52.067,02. *Los operadores estiman ahora que hay un 70 % de probabilidades de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas de interés al menos 25 puntos básicos la próxima semana, frente al 64 % aproximadamente que se estimaba antes del informe del jueves, según la herramienta CME FedWatch. *Tras las recientes caídas, el S&P 500 se sitúa casi un 3 % por debajo de su máximo histórico alcanzado al cierre del 13 de agosto, aunque sigue registrando una subida del 11 % en 2026.

item.title: What comes next in Italy's banking deal frenzy
item.description: The latest twist in Italy's banking takeover saga has pitted market leader Intesa Sanpaolo against the biggest winner of the shakeup so far, Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS).
item.dc:creator: Valentina Za, Gianluca Semeraro
item.content:encoded: The latest twist in Italy's banking takeover saga has pitted market leader Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) against the biggest winner of the shakeup so far, Monte dei Paschi di Siena (BMPS.MI) (MPS). With a less concentrated banking sector than France or Spain, Italy has seen a wave of bids and counterbids since late 2024 as lenders jockey for position amid a revival in dealmaking fuelled by stronger balance sheets and excess capital. The deal frenzy has baffled even seasoned observers, with MPS now pursuing a two-pronged defence strategy to try to fend off Intesa's takeover approach. Intesa on Thursday [USN:L8N4520OF TEXT:"secured shareholder"] approval for the share financing of its plan. Here's where things stand, and what might happen next. WHAT'S THE LATEST? The first merger wave has reshaped Italy's second-tier banking sector, which sits below industry giants Intesa and UniCredit (CRDI.MI) . A long-running political ambition to create a third major group has helped transform MPS, which was rescued by Rome in 2017 and reprivatised in 2023-2024, into an unlikely acquirer. Last year, MPS bought bigger rival Mediobanca and, through that deal, became the leading shareholder in Generali (GASI.MI) , Italy's biggest insurer, which both Intesa and UniCredit covet. After UniCredit [USN:L8N42Q05T TEXT:"built a 9% stake in Generali"] last year, Intesa [USN:L4N42G0DE TEXT:"launched"] its €35 billion ($41 billion) cash-and-shares bid for MPS in June. The deal would give Intesa roughly 13% of Generali, control of Mediobanca and half of MPS's branch network. Critical of Intesa's plan to break up its retail network, MPS initially explored a merger proposed by mid-sized peer Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) [USN:L1N42F03F TEXT:"hours before"] Intesa unveiled its offer. When [USN:L8N4422XY TEXT:"talks with BPM broke down"] last month, MPS responded with all-share bids for both BPM and wealth manager Banca Generali (BGN.MI) . MPS's Generali stake is now key to its [USN:L1N44H0NA TEXT:"defence strategy"]. The bank plans to use part of that holding to reward shareholders, who would receive €3 billion in cash as part of the mainly share-based offer from Intesa. Generali CEO Philippe Donnet has also emerged as an important ally for MPS boss Luigi Lovaglio, with [USN:L8N44O0FV TEXT:"the insurer now open"] to exploring commercial deals with the Tuscan bank. Generali, which competes with Intesa in life insurance, owns 50.2% of Banca Generali and could choose to tender its stake. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? MPS shareholders are due to vote on the defence plan on October 29. Thursday's approval of Intesa's financing plans was widely expected. The real uncertainty now centres on the October vote. Investors remain cautious about MPS' €37 billion twin bids for BPM and Banca Generali, with shares in both targets trading below the offer values. Still, several people close to Intesa told Reuters the scheme had significantly complicated its takeover plans by creating uncertainty and confusing investors. WHAT'S THE COMPLICATION? Intesa is awaiting European Central Bank and antitrust approvals for its bid, with the tender offer expected to begin only after MPS shareholders vote on its defence plan. MPS investors could approve its twin bids and still choose to tender their shares into Intesa's offer. Intesa is counting on completing its offer by the end of December, before MPS has a chance to launch its own bids. COULD UNICREDIT MAKE A MOVE? UniCredit's 9% Generali stake has given it sway in the Intesa-MPS battle. Now that its two-year pursuit of Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) has left it with de facto control of the German lender, UniCredit could refocus on Italy, where it has so far failed to make a mark in the consolidation wave, bankers said. UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel has said he may forego domestic acquisitions rather than overpay. Bankers don't expect Orcel to disrupt Intesa's plans directly, and instead view Banco BPM and Banca Generali as potential targets for UniCredit. WHAT'S THE GOVERNMENT'S STANCE? The government has maintained [USN:L8N44W0N8 TEXT:"a neutral position"] in the latest banking tussle and is not expected to participate in the October vote with its remaining 4.9% stake in MPS. ($1 = 0.8603 euros)

item.title: JD.com's Ceconomy concessions face criticism from rivals, sources say
item.description: JD.com's concessions to ease EU subsidy concerns about the Chinese e-commerce giant's $2.5 billion purchase of German electronics retailer Ceconomy have prompted criticism from competitors, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: JD.com's (9618.HK) concessions to ease EU subsidy concerns about the Chinese e-commerce giant's $2.5 billion purchase of German electronics retailer Ceconomy (CECG.DE) have prompted criticism from competitors, people familiar with the matter told Reuters. They said the European Commission, which acts as the European Union's competition enforcer, informed JD.com earlier this week of the responses to [USN:L1N44H0JY TEXT:"concessions it offered"] last month. The Commission, which will decide on the deal by October 23, and JD.com declined to comment on the negative feedback, which will put pressure on JD.com to improve its concessions. Under its proposals, Ceconomy would access JD.com's European logistics capability and technological capability at market rates, one of the people said. Smaller rivals would also get access at fair and non-discriminatory rates. The EU antitrust watchdog is examining JD.com's proposed acquisition of Ceconomy under the Foreign Subsidies Regulation that targets unfair foreign state aid. Its preliminary review in May indicated that JD.com may have received foreign subsidies such as preferential financing, tax incentives and grants provided by entities possibly attributable to Beijing. The Commission underscored its misgivings by setting out specific concerns in July, which JD.com will have to address in order to gain approval for the deal.

item.title: Finland risks strained power supply after Google AI deal, opposition warns
item.description: Finland should introduce a national permitting system for data centres to prevent the risk of power shortages and soaring energy prices, opposition parties said on Thursday following Google's announcement of a large new investment in the country.
item.dc:creator: Essi Lehto
item.content:encoded: Finland should introduce a national permitting system for data centres to prevent the risk of power shortages and soaring energy prices, opposition parties said on Thursday following Google's announcement of a [USN:L1N4510NH TEXT:"large new investment"] in the country. The Nordic region has for years been a [USN:L6N40I0Y8 TEXT:"magnet for data centres"] thanks to a cool climate, abundant low-carbon electricity and reliable power grids, but AI builders are now facing greater scrutiny from consumers and politicians. Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google said on Wednesday it will spend at least €13 billion ($15.1 billion) on AI infrastructure in Finland over the next two years, its biggest European investment, including a deal for the supply of nuclear power. While data centres are welcome in Finland, the country must make sure there is enough electricity and transmission capacity to power them, Centre Party leader Antti Kaikkonen told Reuters. "A national permitting system for new data centre investments would be needed. At the moment, no one is really looking after the overall picture," said Kaikkonen, whose party is Finland's second-largest opposition group. The Social Democratic Party, which is leading in the polls ahead of an election due in April, said that while it welcomed data centre investments, it remains concerned about the implications for power demand. "It is particularly important that the availability of electricity is also examined as a broader internal security issue, so that people have enough energy and that it is priced at a level they can afford to use," Social Democratic lawmaker Niina Malm said. Google's deal included a 22-year purchase agreement for up to 50% of the energy output from Finland's Loviisa nuclear plant, helping extend the expected life of the plant until 2050, from a previous shutdown date in 2030. The company would also explore the development of new nuclear and renewable energy in Finland alongside utility Fortum (FORTUM.HE) , the two groups said. Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo has said the Google deal will boost the country's economy and that electricity prices will remain under control. The government did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ($1 = 0.8604 euros)

item.title: Monedas cierran mixtas tras datos EEUU que refuerzan apuestas a alza de tasas Fed
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina tuvieron un desempeño dispar al cierre del jueves, en medio de un avance global del dólar tras datos que reforzaron las expectativas de un aumento en las tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos (Fed), en su reunión de política monetaria de la próxima semana.
item.dc:creator: Froilan Romero
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina tuvieron un desempeño dispar al cierre del jueves, en medio de un avance global del dólar tras datos que reforzaron las expectativas de un aumento en las tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos (Fed), en su reunión de política monetaria de la próxima semana. * Los operadores reforzaron sus apuestas a que la Fed subirá las tasas de interés a corto plazo en su reunión de la próxima semana después de que el primer informe clave de inflación de esta semana revelara que los precios al productor en Estados Unidos subieron un 5,4% en los 12 meses hasta agosto. * Las probabilidades de que el banco central estadounidense eleve los tipos de interés un cuarto de punto en su reunión del 15 al 16 de septiembre subieron al 70%, según el precio de los contratos de futuros sobre fondos federales negociados en CME Group, desde un 65% antes del dato. * El Departamento de Trabajo reportó que el número de estadounidenses que solicitaron prestaciones por desempleo descendió la semana pasada, lo que sugiere que los despidos se mantuvieron en niveles bajos y siguieron estabilizando el mercado laboral. * La atención de los mercados se centra ahora en los datos de agosto del índice de precios al consumidor (IPC) que se darán a conocer el viernes en Estados Unidos y que es considerado clave para la decisión de la Fed en materia de tasas de interés. * El índice dólar , que compara a la divisa frente a una canasta de seis monedas de primer orden, escaló alrededor de un 0,2%. * El peso chileno , anotó la mayor caída al ceder un 1,28% y cerrar en 939,80/940,10 por dólar, presionado, además, por una fuerte caída en los precios del cobre, el mayor envío del país. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , perdió un 1,16%, a 11.238,58 puntos. * Los precios del cobre retrocedieron casi un 4% en Londres tras alcanzar un máximo histórico, mientras los operadores sopesan si el repunte de septiembre se había extendido en exceso tras cinco sesiones de avances impulsados por la preocupación ante la reducción de las existencias fuera de Estados Unidos. * El peso mexicano cotizaba al cierre en 16,9996 unidades por dólar, con una pérdida de un 0,64% frente a los 16,8907 pesos del precio de referencia de LSEG del miércoles, debido a un fortalecimiento global del dólar. * El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, bajaba un 1,09%, a 64.1105,20 unidades, arrastrado principalmente por firmas del sector minero ante una caída de los precios de los metales. * El real brasileño se apreció un 0,20%, a 5,1013 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice Bovespa (.BVSP) de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo avanzó un 1,42%, a 188.258,29 puntos. * [USN:L6N4520ZO TEXT:"La actividad del sector"] de servicios de Brasil se mantuvo estable en julio respecto del mes anterior, según datos publicados el jueves por la agencia de estadística IBGE, lo que no cumplió con las expectativas y refuerza los indicios de una desaceleración en la mayor economía de América Latina. * En Argentina, el peso cerró en el mercado interbancario con una apreciación de 0,07% a 1.513 unidades por dólar. La moneda local tocó su nivel mínimo intradiario en la sesión previa al marcar las 1.517,5 unidades para la venta. * En tanto, el índice bursátil Merval (.MERV) de la Bolsa de Buenos Aires avanzó un 1,53%, con lo que acumuló un avance de 4,06% en tres sesiones consecutivas de ganancias. Entre las principales alzas se destacó el sector energético. * El Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Argentina registró una variación de 1,7% en el octavo mes del año, luego del 2,1% de julio, informó el jueves el Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC), cifra que estuvo en línea con las estimaciones del mercado. * El peso colombiano cambió la tendencia de la apertura de la jornada y cerró con una caída de 0,41%, a 3.090 unidades por dólar, mientras que en la bolsa el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) subió 1,65%, a 2.626,71 puntos. * Colombia aumentó en 25 billones de pesos (8.066 millones de dólares) la emisión de títulos de deuda interna para financiar el presupuesto de 2026. El incremento equivale a un 29,3%, desde los 85,25 billones de pesos (27.505 millones de dólares) aprobados inicialmente, de acuerdo con el decreto firmado por el ministro de Hacienda, Miguel Gómez. * La moneda peruana, el sol , cerró la jornada con una merma de 0,51%, a 3,3720/3,3740 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) caía un 1,61%, a 1.559,28 puntos.

item.title: Hungary's central bank may add climate risk scenarios to policy framework
item.description: Hungary's drought and a likely rebound in global food prices could push up inflation next year, central bank Deputy Governor Zoltan Kurali said on Thursday, adding the bank was considering adding climate risk scenarios to its decision-making framework.
item.dc:creator: Gergely Szakacs
item.content:encoded: Hungary's drought and a likely rebound in global food prices could push up inflation next year, central bank Deputy Governor Zoltan Kurali said on Thursday, adding the bank was considering adding climate risk scenarios to its decision-making framework. Record heatwaves and chronic water shortages are [USN:L8N44T097 TEXT:"shrinking maize harvests"] across central and eastern Europe, forcing some farmers to abandon the crop and reshaping a region long viewed as a cornerstone of European grain production. Hungary's Meteorological Service said on Monday the country received its lowest summer rainfall since the start of the 20th century, while median temperatures were the second-highest behind 2024, dealing a blow to agriculture. "The climate effects of the past few years cannot be described along the lines of normal developments," Kurali told an economics conference. "Rather extreme things have played out." He said this year's drought could take a substantial toll on agriculture, hitting the economy and likely adding to price pressures next year from global factors including El Nino and rising food prices driven by higher fuel and fertiliser costs. "The food price trend, which has also contributed significantly to the decline in (Hungarian) inflation, is not necessarily sustainable," Kurali said, referring to previous falls in food prices. The bank, which cut its base rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% last month, as expected, will hold its next policy meeting on September 22, when it is also due to publish updated quarterly forecasts. "We are considering taking the climate issue to the next level in central bank deliberations," Kurali said. He said this would involve permanently incorporating a climate-risk scenario into policymaking and assessing its impact on growth and inflation. However, he highlighted methodological challenges because climate models typically cover much longer periods than the central bank's 18- to 24-month policy horizon.

item.title: Mercados argentinos mejoran, atentos a cifra local de inflación
item.description: La plaza financiera argentina operó mayormente en alza el jueves mientras los inversores centraban su atención en el resultado del dato de inflación de agosto y la próxima licitación de letras del Tesoro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La plaza financiera argentina operó mayormente en alza el jueves mientras los inversores centraban su atención en el resultado del dato de inflación de agosto y la próxima licitación de letras del Tesoro. El Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC) informó que el [USN:ZRN00EJF3 TEXT:"Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC)"] del octavo mes del año fue de 1,7%, mientras que en lo que va del año acumuló un 21,3% y en los últimos 12 meses un 33,5%. El consenso del mercado esperaba un dato de 1,7%, según arrojó un reciente [USN:L1N4510HU TEXT:"sondeo de Reuters"], que coincidió con el [USN:L1N44W0F4 TEXT:"Relevamiento de Expectativas de Mercado (REM)"] del banco central argentino (BCRA). "Hacia adelante, la inflación se mantendrá en un rango de entre 1,5% y 2%", expresó la consultora Wise Capital. Otro factor que impactaba en los inversores es la licitación de títulos del Tesoro argentino que se realizará el viernes, para renovar vencimientos de deuda en moneda local por unos 8,13 billones de pesos. "El Gobierno repite la estrategia utilizada en las últimas dos licitaciones, ofreciendo únicamente bonos que vencen durante la actual administración y limitando la nueva emisión de bonos largos en pesos para evitar una mayor prima por plazo en un contexto de aparente exceso de oferta", dijo la consultora Max Capital. El Tesoro nacional ofrecerá seis títulos que tendrán vencimiento entre octubre de este año y noviembre del 2027. Los bonos en el mercado extrabursátil cerraron el jueves con una mínima caída de 0,1% en promedio, mientras que el riesgo país argentino se ubicaba en 487 puntos básicos. Por su parte, el S&P Merval (.MERV) de la Bolsa de Buenos Aires mejoró un 1,53% a las 2000 GMT, con lo que acumuló un avance de 4,06% en tres sesiones consecutivas en terreno positivo. Entre las principales alzas se destacó el sector energético, con una suba de 2,05% de la petrolera estatal YPF (YPFDm.BA) . YPF colocó [USN:L6N4511DG TEXT:"un bono al 2035 por 1.200 millones de dólares"], según dio a conocer el miércoles tras el cierre del mercado. "La emisión (de YPF) fue la mayor de la compañía desde abril de 2015" explicó Max Capital. "Forma parte de una estrategia de manejo de pasivos, ya que la compañía lanzó una oferta de recompra por hasta 500 millones de dólares de bonos con vencimiento en 2027 y 2029", agregó. La moneda argentina, el peso, cerró en el mercado interbancario con una apreciación de 0,07% a 1.513 unidades por dólar. El peso argentino tocó su nivel mínimo intradiario en la sesión previa al marcar las 1.517,5 unidades para la venta. El [USN:L1N4520OO TEXT:"Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI)"] expresó recientemente que la Argentina debe continuar fortaleciendo sus reservas internacionales, como así también reducir riesgos financieros y preservar el ancla fiscal. El organismo también informó que una misión visitará el país el 21 de septiembre para la tercera revisión del vigente programa con la entidad.

item.title: Fed, eyeing inflation data, may lean toward a hike, traders bet
item.description: The Federal Reserve is a bit more likely to raise short-term borrowing costs at its meeting next week, traders bet on Thursday, after the first of this week's key inflation reports.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve is a bit more likely to raise short-term borrowing costs at its meeting next week, traders bet on Thursday, after the first of this week's key inflation reports. Data showed U.S. [USN:L1N4500SJ TEXT:"producer prices"] rose 5.4% in the 12 months through August, and the country's weekly [USN:L1N4500R4 TEXT:"unemployment insurance claims"] indicated the job market remains stable. Though the overall increase in wholesale prices was in line with what economists had projected, details in the Producer Price Index suggested some of the recent slowing of inflation is being undone as renewed hostilities in the Middle East crimp global oil distribution and the surge in AI investment pushes up demand for electronics. Prices that producers paid for transportation and warehousing jumped in August, the data showed, as did prices for hospital services and airfares. CONSUMER PRICE INDEX IN FOCUS A report on consumer price inflation due on Friday will fill out the inflation picture for Fed officials as they debate whether their policy rate is putting enough downward pressure on inflation to get it to their 2% goal. Inflation has run above the Fed's target for 5-1/2 years. The Fed has kept its policy rate in the 3.50%-3.75% range since December. "With the PPI data overall still looking relatively hot, the Fed seems likely to hike this year even if it doesn’t pull the trigger this month," Capital Economics analysts wrote. As for whether the central bank moves next week, they said, "that still depends on the more important core CPI figure tomorrow." The Fed targets 2% inflation by 12-month change in the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, a data point that can be estimated once CPI and PPI data are in hand. Analysts were divided on Thursday over whether PPI data would push PCE inflation into a range high enough to force the Fed to move next week. Before Thursday's data, traders had seen about a 65% chance of a quarter-point rate hike at the Fed's September 15-16 meeting. That probability is now seen as closer to 70%, based on the price of Fed funds futures contracts traded at CME Group. By year-end, the Fed will almost certainly have delivered one, if not two, interest-rate hikes, market prices imply. The European Central Bank raised its key interest rates earlier on Thursday to stem inflation arising from the Iran war, which has pushed Brent oil futures prices above $100 a barrel.

item.title: US Supreme Court blocks Republican-drawn congressional map in Missouri
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court blocked Missouri on Thursday from using a redrawn congressional map that favors Republicans in November's midterm elections, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump and the party's odds of maintaining its slim majority in the House of Representatives.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Supreme Court blocked Missouri on Thursday from using a redrawn congressional map that favors Republicans in November's midterm elections, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump and the party's odds of maintaining its slim majority in the House of Representatives. The justices granted an emergency request by the map's challengers to suspend a federal judge's decision that allowed only the reconfigured boundaries to be used in the November 3 elections. It was the second time in three days that the nation's highest judicial body rejected bids to preserve the Republican-drawn map in what became an all-out legal fight, waged in both state and federal courts, over Missouri's U.S. House of Representatives districts. Missouri Republicans adopted the new map, which dismantled the Kansas City-based seat of longtime Democratic Representative Emanuel Cleaver, in 2025 as part of a broader effort backed by Trump to redraw congressional districts in ways that could benefit Republican candidates. Following the Supreme Court's action on Thursday, Republican officials said midterm elections would be held under the state's previous congressional map passed in 2022, an outcome they had previously warned would jeopardize their ability to conduct a timely and lawful vote in November. The Supreme Court's brief order was unsigned and gave no explanation, as is common when the justices handle emergency matters. No justice publicly dissented from the decision. The challengers, including a group opposed to the Republican-drawn map called People Not Politicians, had swiftly sought the Supreme Court's intervention after St. Louis, Missouri-based Chief U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark issued his decision on Tuesday. Clark's decision came shortly after the Supreme Court, in a decision made by conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh alone, had [USN:S0N41Y02P TEXT:"declined"] to intervene in a separate bid by Missouri officials to reinstate the redrawn map, which the state's top court had blocked until it is put to a referendum. The judge's order appeared to conflict with the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous September 3 [USN:L1N44V11Z TEXT:"ruling"] blocking the map, leaving the state's congressional districts in limbo and injecting further confusion into the high-stakes electoral fight. Republicans hold a narrow 219-214 majority in the U.S. House, including one independent who caucuses with Republicans. Richard von Glahn, the executive director of People Not Politicians, praised Thursday's decision. "The law is the law, the Missouri constitution is clear as was the Missouri Supreme Court. Over 305,000 Missouri voters — Republicans, Democrats and Independents — took action to block this political power grab last fall," von Glahn said in a statement. "Missouri Republicans have played their last card, and they lost," said Abha Khanna, a lawyer for the group, adding that "Missouri will not be allowed to ram through an egregious gerrymander before the voters have a say." "We respect and will continue to comply with all court decisions," Missouri Republican Attorney General Catherine Hanaway said. The dispute arose when the group collected enough signatures to file for a referendum under a provision in the state constitution that authorizes a ballot measure to approve any legislative act. Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins, the state's top election official, rejected the petition, finding that state constitutional language does not apply to congressional redistricting. The seven-member Missouri Supreme Court, which includes five Republican-appointed judges, disagreed, ruling that the referendum petition was "legal, sufficient, and timely," and that the redrawn map will not take effect until approved by voters. Missouri Republican U.S. Representative Bob Onder and other plaintiffs then filed a lawsuit in federal court seeking to reinstate the Republican-drawn map, leading to Clark's now-suspended order. The fight intensified after Hoskins responded to Clark's order by telling local election officials to proceed with using the 2025 map. The Missouri Supreme Court then said it would consider holding Hoskins in contempt for those actions.

item.title: ABC's Jimmy Kimmel says interview with Senate candidate Talarico will not air on network
item.description: ABC late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel said an interview with Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico on Thursday will air on YouTube and not during the network broadcast, citing threats from the Federal Communications Commission.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: ABC late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel said an interview with Democratic Senate [USN:L6N40L1C8 TEXT:"candidate James Talarico"] on Thursday will air on YouTube and not during the network broadcast, citing threats from the Federal Communications Commission. In January, the Republican-led FCC said that daytime and late-night TV talk shows are no longer considered "bona fide" news programs that are exempt from equal time rules that require them to give airtime to opposing candidates. Kimmel noted that for decades talk shows have been free to interview political candidates without being subject to those rules. Talarico is running in Texas against Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton in a race that could decide control of the U.S. Senate in November. Kimmel noted that he had previously interviewed U.S. President Donald Trump as a candidate in 2016. "Now that he is president, his FCC threatened me, threatened our show, threatened our network ABC, our affiliates, our local stations, based on simple traditional editorial decisions - guest bookings it would seem they don't like," Kimmel said on Wednesday's broadcast. ABC declined to comment. The FCC did not immediately comment. FCC Chair Brendan Carr ordered early reviews in April of Disney's eight [USN:L1N44V0ZX TEXT:"company-owned ABC stations"], even though the license renewals were not scheduled to be considered before October 2028. The FCC had not ordered an early review in more than 50 years before April. The reviews were ordered a day after Trump [USN:S0N40400Q TEXT:"urged ABC to fire Kimmel"]. Disney filed suit to block the early reviews in August, saying Trump is trying to punish the network over its content. Democratic FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez condemned the FCC for saying the agency had intimidated ABC into not airing it. "The FCC has no lawful authority to threaten broadcast licenses over guest bookings or editorial decisions," Gomez said. The FCC is also investigating ABC daytime talk show "The View," which discusses U.S. politics, after saying it is subject to the equal time rules following an interview with Talarico in January. Disney said that since February the program has not invited any political candidates to appear, citing the FCC’s "pressure campaign." In February, former CBS late-night host Stephen Colbert said the network's lawyers barred him from airing an interview with Talarico on his show and instead aired it on YouTube, where it has been seen more than 9.5 million times. Trump has repeatedly urged broadcasters to drop comedy or news programs he dislikes, or which have joked about or criticized him or his administration. He has also called on the FCC to strip stations of licenses after criticizing news and other programming. Broadcast stations need FCC licenses to use public airwaves. While license revocations are extremely rare, critics say the threat of losing a license can pressure broadcasters and raise concerns about government interference in editorial and programming decisions. Networks have broad First Amendment protections over programming choices.

item.title: Proxy solicitor Okapi hires former ISS executive Aicardi
item.description: Proxy solicitor Okapi Partners has hired a former executive from proxy advisory firm Institutional Shareholder Services' (ISS) special situations group, as its clients crave insight into how investors will vote on hotly contested mergers and proxy fights.
item.dc:creator: Svea Herbst-Bayliss
item.content:encoded: Proxy solicitor Okapi Partners has hired a former executive from proxy advisory firm Institutional Shareholder Services' (ISS) special situations group, as its clients crave insight into how investors will vote on hotly contested mergers and proxy fights.
